{{short description|American writer and wildlife biologist}}
'''Marcy Cottrell Houle''' (born August 1, 1953)<ref name=Bio>{{cite book |url= https://books.google.com/books?id=mTSIPaCr2DYC&pg=PA206 |title= Modern American Environmentalists: A Biographical Encyclopedia |editor1-last=Cevasco |editor1-first=George A. |editor2-last=Harmond |editor2-first=Richard P. |year= 2009 |publisher= [[Johns Hopkins University Press]] |chapter= Houle, Marcy Cottrell |last= Schoolman |first= Ethan |pages= 206–211|isbn= 9780801895241 }}</ref> is an American writer and [[wildlife biologist]]. She lives in [[Portland, Oregon]].

==Life and career==
Marcy Houle is a fifth-generation Oregonian, the daughter of George (a prominent orthopedic surgeon) and Margaret Cottrell.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://pages.uoregon.edu/aaarev/Development_News.html|title=Faculty|website=University of Oregon|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120626111929/http://pages.uoregon.edu/aaarev/Development_News.html|archive-date=June 26, 2012 |url-status=dead|accessdate= April 30, 2018}}</ref> When she was born, her family lived on {{convert|13|acre|ha}} of [[old-growth forest]] in [[Neighborhoods of Portland, Oregon|southwest Portland]].<ref name=Bio/> Her early interest in biology was fostered by exploring her own backyard, and she and her two sisters also traveled frequently to [[Vancouver Island]] and backpacked in Oregon forests.<ref name=Bio/>

Houle attended [[Colorado College]] in [[Colorado Springs, Colorado|Colorado Springs]], where she studied [[biology]].<ref name=Bio/> She spent summers after college working for the [[Colorado Parks and Wildlife|Colorado Division of Wildlife]] studying [[peregrine falcon]]s near [[Chimney Rock National Monument]], an experience she documented in her 1991 book ''[[Wings for My Flight: The Peregrine Falcons of Chimney Rock]]''.<ref name=Bio/> She married John Houle in 1982; they lived on [[Sauvie Island]].<ref name=Bio/> After enrolling in [[Oregon State University]] to earn a [[Master's degree|master's]] in biology, she studied [[Bird of prey|raptor]]s on [[Zumwalt Prairie]] for the [[United States Fish and Wildlife Service|U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service]], an experience she documented in her 1995 book ''[[The Prairie Keepers|The Prairie Keepers: Secrets of the Zumwalt]]''.<ref name=Bio/> Her research there helped lead to the prairie becoming a nature preserve.<ref name=Bio/>

Houle's 30-year interest in [[Forest Park (Portland, Oregon)|Forest Park]] in Portland culminated in a wildlife and vegetation study that the [[Oregon Historical Society]] (OHS) published in 1988 as ''One City's Wilderness: Portland's Forest Park''.<ref name="End Notes"/> OHS published a second edition of the book in 1996, and in 2010 [[Oregon State University Press]] published the third edition. The third edition includes maps of the park by cartographer Erik Goetze and images by photographers Gerry Carr and Lois Miller.<ref name="End Notes">{{cite book|author=Houle, Marcy Cottrell|title=One City's Wilderness: Portland's Forest Park|publisher=Oregon State University Press|location=Corvallis, Oregon|year=2010|edition=3rd|isbn=978-0-87071-588-4|oclc= 544474594 |lccn=2010007205}}</ref>

In addition to ''Wings for My Flight'' and ''One City's Wilderness'', her publications include a third book, ''The Prairie Keepers: Secrets of the Zumwalt''. Her work has also appeared in ''The Nature Conservancy Magazine'', ''Reader's Digest'', ''The New York Times'', and other periodicals.<ref name="End Notes"/>

==Awards and honors==
''Wings for My Flight'' was awarded an [[Oregon Book Award]] for [[Creative nonfiction|literary nonfiction]] in 1991, a [[Christopher Award]] in 1992, and the same year [[New York Public Library]] named the book one of the Best Books for the Teenaged.<ref name=Bio/>

''The Prairie Keepers'' was named a ''[[Booklist]]'' Editor's Choice. It was also named an Earth Day Reader's Selection by ''The New York Times''.<ref>{{cite web|title=The Prairie Keepers: Secrets of the Zumwalt|publisher=Oregon State University Press|url=http://osupress.oregonstate.edu/book/prairie-keepers|accessdate=November 13, 2014}}</ref>

* ''A Generous Nature: Lives Transformed by Oregon'' (2019)
* ''Forest Park: Exploring Portland's Natural Sanctuary'' (2023)
